meta.name: SDE1 / SDE2 interview roadmap
meta.basedOn: Sequence adapted from Tech Interview Handbook (yangshun) and takeUforward's interview roadmap: resume/profiles first, CS core + DSA in parallel, behavioral bank before the Jan 8 job-search start, applications + OA tracking through the Jan–Feb 2027 search window. Prioritize main-language depth, concurrency basics, database correctness, testing/debugging and security for both levels. SDE2/backend adds database performance, distributed failures and operational ownership. Android, frontend, framework internals, advanced algorithms and AI/FDE are role-dependent.

sources.title: Tech Interview Handbook
sources.note: The master flow this roadmap follows

sources.title: takeUforward — Striver's SDE Sheet page
sources.note: Reference for the Indian-market interview loop

phases.name: CS Core
phases.desc: OS, DBMS, networking and OOP foundations for both levels. Apply these through the dedicated concurrency, language, security and testing sections; extend database depth for SDE2/backend.

items.title: OS: processes vs threads, scheduling, context switching
OS: synchronization — mutex/semaphore, deadlock (conditions, prevention)
OS: memory — paging, segmentation, virtual memory, thrashing
DBMS: normalization (1NF→BCNF), keys, ER model
DBMS: transactions — ACID, isolation levels, concurrency control, locks
DBMS: indexing — B+ trees, clustered vs non-clustered
CN: OSI vs TCP/IP layers, what happens when you type a URL
CN: TCP vs UDP, 3-way handshake, congestion control basics
CN: HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, TLS handshake, cookies vs sessions
OOP: 4 pillars with real code examples in your main language
OOP: interfaces vs abstract classes, composition vs inheritance
OOP: common follow-ups — static/final, overloading vs overriding, virtual functions
Database correctness: unique, foreign-key and check constraints; enforce invariants in the database
Transaction anomalies: dirty, non-repeatable and phantom reads, lost updates and write skew; compare behavior in your database at each isolation level
Locking strategies: optimistic version columns and conditional updates versus pessimistic row locks
Index design: composite column order, selectivity, covering indexes, read benefits and write costs
Query execution: read an execution plan; compare scans, index access, expensive joins and sorts
Application/database boundaries: N+1 queries, connection pools, transaction boundaries and long transactions
Pagination: offset versus keyset, stable ordering and concurrent inserts
SDE2/backend — MVCC: row versions, reader snapshots and interaction with locking
SDE2/backend — recovery: write-ahead logging and crash recovery conceptually

phases.name: Main-language depth
phases.desc: Essential for both levels. Choose one main language and use its branch below as a guide; the common checklist applies only to that language.

items.title: Equality and hashing contracts; mutability, copying, references and parameter passing
Collection internals and operation costs; comparators and ordering
Exceptions and resource cleanup; generics and type-system basics
Memory management: garbage collection or ownership/lifetimes in your language
Concurrency and async model: explain execution, synchronization and cancellation in your language

branches.name: Java / Kotlin
branches.detail: equals/hashCode, collections, generics, garbage collection and synchronization; Kotlin nullability and coroutines.

branches.name: Python
branches.detail: Mutability, hashability, iterators/generators, exceptions, GIL implications for your runtime, threading versus multiprocessing versus asyncio.

branches.name: JavaScript / TypeScript
branches.detail: Closures, event loop/microtasks, promises, reference equality, runtime versus static types.

branches.name: C++
branches.detail: RAII, ownership, smart pointers, copy/move semantics, STL complexity and iterator invalidation.

phases.name: Practical concurrency
phases.desc: Both levels: races, locking, deadlocks and producer–consumer. SDE2/backend: visibility, atomics, pools, cancellation and service-level correctness.

items.title: Race conditions and atomicity: demonstrate why a safe check followed by a safe update can still race
Locks, mutexes, semaphores and producer–consumer with a bounded queue
Deadlock, starvation, livelock and lock contention; consistent lock ordering
Async I/O versus parallel execution: what each solves and what it does not
SDE2/backend — visibility and ordering: the memory-model guarantees in your language
SDE2/backend — read/write locks, atomics, compare-and-swap and condition variables
SDE2/backend — thread pools, futures/promises, cancellation and timeouts
Last-seat exercise: protect check-and-reserve in one process, then across multiple servers using database transactions or conditional updates

phases.name: Application security
phases.desc: Essential for both levels; go deeper for backend/full-stack. Explain how an ordinary application protects accounts, APIs and data.

items.title: Authentication versus authorization; object-level checks so users cannot access another user’s resource
Sessions versus tokens; JWT expiry, validation and revocation trade-offs
OAuth 2.0 versus OpenID Connect conceptually
Password hashing versus encryption
SQL injection and parameterized queries
XSS, CSRF and what CORS does and does not protect
Secrets management, least privilege and keeping sensitive data out of logs

phases.name: Testing, debugging & engineering lifecycle
phases.desc: Essential testing/debugging for both levels. Apply failure-path reasoning independently of timed practice; deepen operational delivery for SDE2.

items.title: Unit, integration and end-to-end tests; test doubles, mocks and dependency boundaries
Boundary-value and failure-path testing, including dependency failures
Debug with logs, stack traces, metrics and profiling
Diagnose slow APIs, slow queries and memory growth
CI/CD basics, backward-compatible changes, rollback and feature flags

phases.name: SQL
phases.desc: LeetCode SQL 50 is a solid foundation, not an exhaustive guarantee of OA coverage. Keep joins, aggregations, subqueries and window functions; connect them to query plans and indexes in CS Core.

items.title: SQL 50: Select (5 problems)
SQL 50: Basic Joins (9 problems)
SQL 50: Basic Aggregate Functions (8 problems)
SQL 50: Sorting and Grouping (7 problems)
SQL 50: Advanced Select and Joins (7 problems)
SQL 50: Subqueries (7 problems)
SQL 50: Advanced String Functions / Regex / Clause (7 problems)
Revision: window functions (RANK, ROW_NUMBER, LAG/LEAD) beyond SQL 50

items.title: LinkedIn: headline with target role + stack, About with metrics, featured projects, open-to-work (recruiters only)
Naukri: complete profile to 100%, headline keywords, ⟳ REFRESH WEEKLY (resurfaces you in recruiter search — mark revisit to auto-remind)

phases.name: Behavioral — STAR bank
phases.desc: Write answers as Situation-Task-Action-Result. Notes field on each question = your answer. Rehearse aloud once a week from mid-Aug.

items.title: Tell me about yourself (90-second version)
Most challenging project / hardest technical problem you solved
A time you disagreed with a teammate or senior — how did you resolve it?
A mistake or failure — what did you learn and change?
A time you had to learn something quickly to deliver
A time you took ownership beyond your role
Handling a tight deadline / multiple priorities
A time you received hard feedback — how did you respond?
Why are you leaving your current company? (never negative)
Why this company / role? (research template: product, stack, one specific thing)
Questions to ask the interviewer (prepare 3 per round type)
SDE2 — clarify ambiguous requirements and explain the trade-offs you chose
SDE2 — handle an operational incident: diagnosis, mitigation, recovery and prevention
SDE2 — coordinate across teams and help other engineers through reviews or mentoring
